story_type: Soyuz launch and spacecraft separation seen from an onboard camera
hook: This camera rode a rocket to space and watched its ship break free.
narration: This camera rode a Russian rocket to space and watched its cargo ship break free.
The ship was Progress 89, launching from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan on August fourteenth, twenty twenty-four.
Four strap-on boosters and the core stage all light together on the pad.
Nobody was aboard. Packed inside the nose were more than three tons of supplies and cargo for the space station.
A Soyuz throws away each stage as it runs dry, so the rocket gets lighter and faster all the way up.
[short pause] Once it was free, the ship's solar panels swung open.
outcome: Progress 89 made it to orbit and headed for the space station with its cargo.
title: Rocket cam watches its cargo ship break free
description:
The uncrewed Roscosmos Progress 89 cargo spacecraft launched toward the International Space Station on a Soyuz rocket from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan on Aug. 14, 2024, carrying over three tons of supplies and cargo. A camera on the rocket watched the spacecraft separate in orbit.
